newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas prices rise on cold weather.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas prices rise on cold weather.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices rose sharply Monday, led by expectations for colder temperatures later this week, market sources said.

At the AECO storage hub, prices for Tuesday delivery were around C$2.03 per gigajoule (GJ) early and near C$2.20 late. Trader said most deals were done in the C$2.15-2.16 area, up an average of 13 cents from Friday.
Despite seasonable temperatures now in Alberta, forecasters are calling for a return to colder weather by midweek.
February/March business at AECO was talked in the C$2.15-2.20 per GJ range, while for the remainder of the winter, prices hovered in the C$2.07-2.10 range.
July/August prices were in the C$1.58-1.60 area, traders said.
At Sumas, Wash., prices soared into the $3.05-3.30 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) range, up more than a $1 from Friday.

A factor contributing to the sharp uptick were significantly stronger California prices, sources said. At Topock, the southern California border, prices surged to about $3.90 per mmBtu, up about $1.40 from Friday's levels. High winds in the area resulted in about 75,000 Southern California Edison customers without power service.
At Niagara, the eastern Canadian export point, prices rose by more than 60 cents to the $3.70s per mmBtu, with trades ranging anywhere from $3.50 to the $3.90s.
